title: Unsloth's NVFP4 Qwen3.6 Quants Beat NVIDIA's Own — by Actually Using 4-bit Math
hook: Unsloth's NVFP4 quants for Qwen3.6 run up to 2.5x faster than NVIDIA's official NVFP4 release, with no measured accuracy loss — by quantizing activations too, not just weights.
key_points: Unsloth's NVFP4 quants for Qwen3.6-27B run 2.5x faster than NVIDIA's own NVFP4 quants; the 35B-A3B variant is 1.56x-1.79x faster.
The speedup comes from true W4A4 (4-bit weights AND activations, using 4-bit tensor cores), versus NVIDIA's W4A16 (4-bit weights, 16-bit activations).
Validated on MMLU-Pro, AIME 2025, and GPQA against FP8, BF16, and NVIDIA's NVFP4, with no reported accuracy degradation.
Bundled FP8 KV-cache calibration roughly doubles usable context length.
Ships a fast/accuracy trade-off pair for the 35B-A3B model: NVFP4-Fast (full W4A4, 1.79x) and NVFP4 (1.56x).
content_html: NVIDIA shipped official NVFP4 quants for Qwen3.6. Unsloth's own NVFP4 quants for the same model are faster still — up to 2.5x on the 27B model — without giving up accuracy.
extra_html: The gap comes down to what actually gets quantized. NVIDIA's NVFP4 release keeps activations at 16-bit precision (W4A16); Unsloth's quants use true W4A4 — 4-bit weights and 4-bit activations — so matrix multiplies run on real 4-bit tensor cores instead of falling back to wider math. Unsloth reports 2.5x faster inference for Qwen3.6-27B and 1.56x-1.79x for 35B-A3B (offering both a full-speed "NVFP4-Fast" and a slightly more conservative "NVFP4" variant), validated with no accuracy degradation on MMLU-Pro, AIME 2025, and GPQA against FP8, BF16, and NVIDIA's NVFP4. The release also bundles FP8 KV-cache calibration, roughly doubling usable context length, and comes with Multi-Token Prediction pre-embedded. Posted by Unsloth co-founder Daniel Han to r/LocalLLaMA, 2026-07-10.

related.title: Gemma 4 QAT: 4-Bit Weights That Keep Their Quality
related.hook: Squeezing a model to 4 bits after training loses quality. Quantization-aware training bakes the rounding into training instead — and Google shipped Gemma 4 checkpoints that do exactly that.

related.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Why 'Same Accuracy' Doesn't Mean 'Same Model'
related.hook: Two quantized models can score identically on accuracy while disagreeing on which individual examples they get right — a gap standard benchmarks are structurally blind to.
